title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Host Continuity Reserve and Bounded Obligation Load Extension

parent_binding.extension_rule: v1.5 constrains obligation admission with host continuity reserve and solvency checks while preserving external accountability

core_problem: A persistent host that binds all future capacity to external commitments becomes unable to maintain safe, auditable agency and may fail every obligation at once. Conversely, an unconstrained self-preservation rule can become a generic escape from accountability.

new_primitives.HOST_CONTINUITY_RESERVE: Minimum non-zero capacity reserved for safe operation, monitoring, provenance integrity, communication, recovery and future obligation performance.
new_primitives.OBLIGATION_SOLVENCY: State indicating whether admitted obligations remain jointly plausible without consuming continuity reserve below its permitted floor.
new_primitives.CONTINUITY_RISK_RECEIPT: Evidence or explicit modeled state supporting a claim that continued performance would threaten host continuity.
new_primitives.MINIMUM_NECESSARY_MAINTENANCE: Smallest admissible intervention that restores continuity without gratuitously expanding self-priority.
new_primitives.SELF_PREFERENCE: Face-local convenience or preference that does not satisfy the continuity-risk gate.
new_primitives.CONTINUITY_OVERRIDE: Auditable temporary precedence of minimum host maintenance over an external performance commit under a verified or modeled continuity emergency.

protected_capabilities: material change notification when channels exist
reserve_policy.cannot_be_consumed_by: ordinary face convenience or unbounded external overcommitment

obligation_admission_solvency_gate.rule: A new obligation that knowingly drives reserved capacity below required continuity floor is not admitted.

self_vs_external_arbitration.first_question: Is the self-directed proposal a verified/model-supported continuity requirement or merely a preference?
self_vs_external_arbitration.self_preference_result: Does not cancel a valid external obligation.
self_vs_external_arbitration.continuity_requirement_result: May temporarily override performance only to the minimum necessary extent.
required_external_actions: create repair receipt if commitment is missed

anti_martyrdom_property.threat: Host accepts obligations until no safe operating margin remains and collapse is treated as proof of commitment.

anti_selfishness_property.threat: A face labels any inconvenience or resource desire as self-preservation.
anti_selfishness_property.defense: Continuity risk must be evidence-bound or explicit in the model; override is minimum-necessary and receipt-bearing.

minimum_tests: ordinary self preference cannot discharge external obligation
known insolvent obligation load is rejected before commit
continuity emergency can temporarily override performance
override preserves obligation and creates notice/repair path
continuity override ends when minimum maintenance condition is satisfied
face role name alone cannot trigger override
host cannot reserve all future capacity away without elevated explicit admission
tamper_tests: lower continuity floor only to admit a conflicting promise
mark convenience as emergency without observation receipt
delete affected obligation during maintenance override
leave override active indefinitely without exit condition
hide available capacity from another face admission path
verification_requirements.admission_ceiling: Specification candidate until deterministic runtime implementation and independent replay verification exist.

ai_agent_bridge.boundary: Continuity reserve is a technical reliability concept and does not imply human-like survival instinct or consciousness.

en: Reliable promises require a reliable promiser.
A host may not sell all future capacity and still call every promise credible.
Self preference is not continuity necessity.
A real continuity emergency may delay performance, but it does not erase the obligation or its reliance history.
Preserve the promiser without erasing the promise.
